name: Ilex

project_scope.selection_mode: Three already installed canonical species; genus lesson added independently of species installer
project_scope.source_pool: Genus Study Index row 8; canonical manifest
project_scope.native_status_boundary: Ilex opaca is retained as a nursery-trade/encounter comparison, not confirmed target-zone native; preserve all species range statuses

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: Start on an intact twig, not the red fruit. First ask whether leaves drop in winter. On evergreen plants, compare leaf size, thickness and whether marginal teeth are rounded scallops or sharp, stiff spine tips. For genus confirmation, inspect tiny axillary flowers and a mature drupe with several hard pyrenes.
shared_traits: Woody shrubs or trees with alternate, simple, stipulate-appearing but typically inconspicuous stipule structures; branchlets may carry clustered flowers and fruit.
Small usually 4–5-parted axillary flowers, often functionally unisexual on different individuals (usually dioecious).
Fruit is a small fleshy drupe containing multiple hard pyrenes, not a botanically true berry.
All three species may bear red fruit; red berries alone do not prove species or even genus.
shared_genus_recognition.image_first_guidance: Match winter twig silhouette to close-up of the leaf margin, then add fruit/flower anatomy confirmation; for leafless possumhaw seek a documented seasonal comparison.

species_comparison_matrix.Ilex decidua: DECIDUOUS: often leafless while fruit persists in winter
Moderate, thin elliptic–obovate/spatulate leaves; larger than typical yaupon
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex opaca: Large, thick evergreen leaves, markedly larger than typical yaupon

species_comparison_matrix.Ilex decidua: Soft shallow crenate to crenate-serrate teeth; not sharp spines
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex vomitoria: Low rounded crenate/scalloped teeth; not strongly spiny
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex opaca: Stiff, sharp, spine-tipped marginal teeth on many mature leaves

species_comparison_matrix.Ilex decidua: Relatively thin deciduous foliage; shrub/small tree, pale gray twigs
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex vomitoria: Small leathery leaves, often multistemmed shrub to small tree
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex opaca: Very leathery large glossy leaves; evergreen tree, often pyramidal when young

species_comparison_matrix.Ilex decidua: Small axillary, usually functionally unisexual flowers; identify pistillate vs staminate structures
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex vomitoria: Small axillary unisexual white flowers; dioecious
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex opaca: Small axillary unisexual pale flowers; dioecious
species_comparison_matrix.weight: GENUS confirmation, not primary species separator

species_comparison_matrix.Ilex decidua: Red/orange drupes frequently remain visible on leafless winter twigs
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex vomitoria: Persistent bright red drupes among small evergreen leaves
species_comparison_matrix.Ilex opaca: Red drupes among large evergreen spiny leaves
species_comparison_matrix.weight: SECONDARY; fruit color shared and insufficient

look_here_first_sequence.look: full winter twig plus matched growing-season leaf
look_here_first_sequence.decision: If winter deciduous with orange/red drupes on bare twigs, favor I. decidua; confirm soft toothed thin leaves from appropriate season.

look_here_first_sequence.look: evergreen shoot with ruler at mid-stem leaves
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Small 1–4 cm blades with low rounded crenations favor I. vomitoria; very large thick blades with rigid spine-tipped teeth favor I. opaca.

look_here_first_sequence.look: leaf margin at macro scale and lower leaf surface
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Separate rounded crenations from stiff spines; damaged, juvenile and shade leaves may vary.

look_here_first_sequence.look: flower sex plus ripe drupe cross-section
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Verify staminate vs pistillate flowers and the multiple pyrenes to reinforce Ilex; do not treat fruiting sex as a species split.

look_here_first_sequence.look: ambiguous urban ornamental or juvenile sterile shoot
look_here_first_sequence.decision: Mark Ilex sp. or cultivated-holly comparison pending flowering/leaf characters; landscape planting is not evidence of native range.

cautions: I. opaca is already retained as a canonical LOOKALIKE_COMPARISON; its Texas state-level range does not qualify it as confirmed native in the project's target counties. Do not include in native-only counts.
Some American holly leaves vary in spine count, including nearly spineless older branches. Require overall blade size/texture and twig context, not one tooth.
Leaf margins of many hollies change between juvenile and mature branches; use several mature, intact leaves.
Only pistillate plants with successful pollination bear abundant fruit; absence of red drupes does not exclude any of these species.
Possumhaw's winter fruit display is seasonal and sex-specific. An in-leaf summer possumhaw may need leaf texture and twig comparison.
The fruit is a drupe with hard pyrenes; teach the botanical distinction from true berries.
No original species taxonomy, range state, or media attribution was changed in this lesson.

local_lookalikes.separate: Check horn-like leaf teeth, proportions and planted context; do not equate spines with I. opaca alone.
Small crenate evergreen leaves can mimic yaupon; check fruit color/architecture, leaf arrangement and nursery origin; avoid a county-native inference.
Follow calyx and fruit: Diospyros produces larger berry-type fruits with a conspicuous persistent calyx, not multiple hard holly pyrenes.
Require alternate leaves, Ilex axillary flowers and drupe pyrenes; red fruit is a poor first clue.
